Potential security risk (IP, browser, OS and other data leaking) versus discomfort. One is worse.

I have Irlen syndrome. Basically, my brain doesn't process printed text on certain color backgrounds correctly. One of the symptoms is that glare can be painful. For whatever reason, black on white is better than white on black because my brain says "Little bright points of light! Ow, glare!" So nightmode causes me physical pain.

For the most part, my other security measures takes care of IP logging for offsite CSS images and similar avenues of abuse. Not that they'll get the correct IP anyway. But, no, the CSS rules generally aren't applied if you turn it off. There are two possible mechanisms for this:

  1. The CSS just isn't injected.

  2. A parent element for the page gets a specific class or attribute which is injected into the custom CSS. This would allow the CSS to be applied. If the custom class or attribute is not on the element but still injected into the custom CSS, the CSS code would be there but not applied (and therefore not executed). I had to do something similar for boilerplate code where something like 7 different sites used the same layout and mechanics but had different colors and images.
